newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish newsprint prices fall 2-5 pct from Sept 1.
newsitem.headline: Swedish newsprint prices fall 2-5 pct from Sept 1.

text.p: A Swedish newspaper publishers' group said on Thursday that newsprint prices would be cut by two to five percent from September 1 and would be reconsidered at year-end.
The price cut was the result of discussions between the publishers' association TU and Sweden's major paper producing companies, Stora, MoDo and SCA.
"This lowering was wanted but not expected," Sune Lund, chairman of TU, told Reuters.
"At the end of the year we will negotiate an agreement and the trend is for prices to continue coming down."
The TU purchasing group represents 70 newspapers which together account for half of the total annual newsprint consumption in Sweden of 400,000 tonnes.
The cut in newsprint paper by two to five percent from September 1 had been forecast by forestry group Stora.
"This cut is exactly what we forecast at the shareholders' meeting," Stora managing director Lars-Ake Helgesson told Reuters.
He would not say if the price cuts would continue.
Goran Lundin from forestry group Modo's Holmen paper group said it was the right time to lower prices considering current demand.
U.S. newsprint prices fell substantially in the spring this year, by about 17 percent, and are lower than in Europe.
Lundin said it was not yet really relevant to compare the prices in the U.S. with those in Europe.
"In the U.S. you have a completely different contract system where one negotiates agreements conseriderably more often," Lundin said.
"Seen over the economic cycle there is not a big price difference between between the U.S. and Europe."
